chapter: Touring in the bus years and Jim Crow in the South
title: White men attack Warren Luckey and Fields is hit with a tire tool
summary: A crowd follows the two musicians out; Luckey fights back, and Fields, trying to intervene, is struck, until a station owner threatens the attackers.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: And so the boys--they never did open their mouth--they got the sandwich and paid and came on out. When they came out, four or five cats came following them--
Yeah, white guys were following them, and when they got on this vacant
lot kind of, one of them grabbed them, one of them picked up a stick and hit Warren with it and Warren took that stick away from him and boy, went to working him over.

So I got my pistol and not to get everybody killed, I handed--I thought Parker would be the coolest one--I said don't do anything unless they start for this bus, and I got out of the bus and I started for the proprietor in there, and I said, do something, say something, you see the boys weren't bothering them and I guess me getting hit is what made it stop, because the guys in the bus said when they saw that man (inaudible), but a guy was slipping up behind me with a tire tool and Estelle said, Ernie, look out, and I didn't know what way he was coming from but I happened to dodge the right way and he hit me just a little and knocked me down and when he knocked me down, that guy walked out the filling station and said, if another one of you raise your hand at them boys, I'll blow you in two, they're not bothering you.

Some guys had been jumping off a city bus, a city bus drove up and they jumped off to help these guys and he said you better get off that bus and get away from here and you all that came out of that cafe better get back in there, or off of my property. You better not raise another hand.
There was always some right person.
